## 型

### Map

```emela
opaque enum Map[K, V]
```

A map from keys of type `K` to values of type `V`, ordered by the keys.

## 値

### empty

```emela
fn empty[K, V]() -> Map[K, V]
```

The empty map.

### from_list

```emela
fn from_list[K: Ord, V](pairs: List[(K, V)]) -> Map[K, V]
```

The map of the pairs. A key given twice takes its later value.

### insert

```emela
fn insert[K: Ord, V](m: Map[K, V], key: K, value: V) -> Map[K, V]
```

`m` with `key` mapped to `value`, replacing its value if it is there.

### remove

```emela
fn remove[K: Ord, V](m: Map[K, V], key: K) -> Map[K, V]
```

`m` without `key`. The same map if `key` is not there.

### update

```emela
fn update[K: Ord, V](m: Map[K, V], key: K, f: fn(Option[V]) -> Option[V] fails E(f) uses { R(f) }) -> Map[K, V] fails E(f) uses { R(f) }
```

`f` gets the value of `key` (`None` if it is not there). `Some` sets the value, and `None`
removes the key.

### get

```emela
fn get[K: Ord, V](m: Map[K, V], key: K) -> Option[V]
```

The value of `key`.

### contains

```emela
fn contains[K: Ord, V](m: Map[K, V], key: K) -> Bool
```

Whether `key` is in `m`.

### size

```emela
fn size[K, V](m: Map[K, V]) -> Int
```

The number of keys.

### is_empty

```emela
fn is_empty[K, V](m: Map[K, V]) -> Bool
```

### fold

```emela
fn fold[K, V, B](m: Map[K, V], from: B, f: fn(B, K, V) -> B fails E(f) uses { R(f) }) -> B fails E(f) uses { R(f) }
```

Folds the pairs in key order, starting from `from`.

### each

```emela
fn each[K, V](m: Map[K, V], f: fn(K, V) -> () fails E(f) uses { R(f) }) -> () fails E(f) uses { R(f) }
```

Calls `f` on each pair in key order. Stops at the first failure.

### to_list

```emela
fn to_list[K, V](m: Map[K, V]) -> List[(K, V)]
```

The pairs in key order.

### keys

```emela
fn keys[K, V](m: Map[K, V]) -> List[K]
```

The keys in order.

### values

```emela
fn values[K, V](m: Map[K, V]) -> List[V]
```

The values in key order.

### map_values

```emela
fn map_values[K, V, W](m: Map[K, V], f: fn(V) -> W fails E(f) uses { R(f) }) -> Map[K, W] fails E(f) uses { R(f) }
```

`f` on each value. The keys stay. `f` is called in key order (`[lib.api-rules]`), so the left
subtree is built before the value of the node, and the right one after it.

### filter

```emela
fn filter[K, V](m: Map[K, V], f: fn(K, V) -> Bool fails E(f) uses { R(f) }) -> Map[K, V] fails E(f) uses { R(f) }
```

The pairs for which `f` is True.

### union

```emela
fn union[K: Ord, V](a: Map[K, V], b: Map[K, V]) -> Map[K, V]
```

The keys of both. A key in both takes its value in `a` (as in Haskell's `Data.Map.union`).
